collection.description: The stories also say that a moon shell worn at the throat for one full moon brings a child, and sometimes more than one.

ask.text:
(friend) has found a moon shell on the reef: round, white and shining, the kind the old stories say the sea spirit gives to women she favours. The stories also say that a moon shell worn at the throat for one full moon brings a child, and sometimes more than one. (friend) has strung it on a cord, and holds it out to (subject).
(subject) and (friend) have talked about a family, but haven't decided. Should she wear it, or hang it in the doorway as a charm for the hut instead?

c1o1.text: At the end of the month, (subject) is pregnant. The midwives, feeling her belly a few weeks later, look at each other and grin: {#babies:one strong baby, they say, a real kicker|twins|triplets}. "The stories said sometimes more than one," says (friend) faintly. "I thought that was just the stories." The moon shell goes in the {#babies:baby's|babies'|babies'} basket.

c1o2.text: At the end of the month, (subject) is pregnant with one baby, and gives the moon shell back to the sea, as the stories say she should, with a thank-you. (friend) rows her out to the reef to do it. They watch the white shell sink slowly into the blue until they can't see it any more.

c1.text: (subject) ties the cord around her neck. The shell is cool against her skin, and for the whole month it never once gets warm, even in the midday sun...

c2o1.text: It seems the sea spirit isn't fussy about where her shell is hung. A few weeks later, (subject) is pregnant anyway. "It's the doorway," the oldest midwife says knowingly. "Everyone walks through a doorway." (friend) looks at the shell with new respect.

c2o2.text: Nothing happens for (subject). But (neighbour), who lives next door and has walked past that doorway every day for a month, is suddenly pregnant, and not a little surprised. (subject) and (friend) decide that's a fine use for a moon shell, and give it to (neighbour) to keep for the baby.

c2.text: (subject) hangs the moon shell in the doorway, where it turns slowly in the breeze and catches the light every evening...
